messages:
sara-docs: quick heads-up — opened a doc PR that adds a connection-flow diagram for the private installer + an SDK endpoint-override snippet for air-gapped setups. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-docs/pull/12876

sara-docs: main goals: clarify which ports need to be open for KMS/HSM tunnels, show where to drop cert bundles in airgap, and provide a tiny python/curl example to hit a private control plane.

matt-ops: nice, will review. can you include the minimal ACLs we tested with the HSM (PKCS#11 unix socket + 1793/tcp for kms-relay)?

sara-docs: yes — added a note + example firewall rules. shortened version in the PR: ``
# iptables example (host receiving kms proxy)
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 1793 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m unix -p all -m comment --comment "allow pkcs11 socket" -j ACCEPT
``

devon-sec: re: unix socket rule — we can't match unix sockets with iptables. maybe rephrase to recommend file system permissions + systemd unit options. also flag: HSM vendors sometimes bind to an abstract socket; mention both.

sara-docs: good catch. updated the text to mention filesystem perms + systemd ProtectHome= and a note about abstract sockets. thanks.

matt-ops: also add a small connectivity diag for VPC peering + NAT path. some customers get confused where the control plane egress comes from. a simple ascii helps.

sara-docs: added: ``
[onprem subnet] --(peering)-> [mgmt VPC] --(NAT)-> [internet/proxy]
``

olga-release: small nit: link to the dedicated installer binary checksum page is broken in your PR (404). search docs repo for /installer/checksums.md and update.

sara-docs: ack — fixed link to /installer/checksums.yml and added a redirect note.

infra-bot: deploy-check: docs lint passed for changed files (scripts/validate-links), 0 warnings.

devon-sec: can you add a short snippet showing how to configure SDK to use a local control-plane URL? like one-liner for curl + python.

sara-docs: put this in the PR under "SDK examples (air-gapped)":
``
# curl (control plane running at 10.0.0.4)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -X POST https://10.0.0.4/api/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}'

# python (requests)
import requests
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
resp = requests.post("https://10.0.0.4/api/v1/generate", json={"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())
``

matt-ops: perfect. also add a short compatibility table row: RHEL 8.7 vs 9.1 vs Ubuntu 22.04 for the offline installer. customers ask that a lot.

sara-docs: added a tiny matrix with tested distros + kernel reqs. left TODO to expand test matrix later.

olga-release: can we include a short rollback paragraph for the installer? docs should say how to revert certificate bundle or switch back to hosted control plane.

sara-docs: added rollback steps: save current certs, swap symlink back to /etc/redwood/control-ca, restart redwood-agent, and a note to check agents status.

devon-sec: one last sec note — call out that KMS traffic must be authenticated with mTLS when talking to our kms-relay; include the sample curl with --cert/--key.

sara-docs: updated with mTLS snippet. final checklist in PR: link fixes, firewall example fixes (remove unix iptables bit), ascii diag, sdk examples, distro matrix, rollback steps. tagging reviewers @matt-ops @devon-sec @olga-release. :raised_hands:
